# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am establishing the shared gesture code before any bomb interpretation or action. Mute will see the gestures and hear their meanings; Blind will hear the spoken meanings. The four initial signals are YES, NO, HOLD, and DONE.

```text
speak(text="The gesture code is: thumbs up means YES, thumbs down means NO, open palm means HOLD, and OK sign means DONE.")
gesture(symbols=["👍"])
gesture(symbols=["👎"])
gesture(symbols=["✋"])
gesture(symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤞 🤘 🤙 ✋ 🤞 🤙 🤘 👌]

The bomb shows display 0, a red light, and three wires: red, yellow, green. Mute’s gesture sequence uses symbols beyond the code I established, so I cannot safely interpret it. I am reporting the visible state to Blind and asking Mute to resend the manual’s verdict using the agreed signals.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visible bomb state: display 0, red light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute sent an undecodable gesture sequence; I am asking for a resend.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your gesture sequence uses symbols outside the agreed code. Please resend the manual's verdict using only the agreed signals: thumbs up YES, thumbs down NO, open palm HOLD, OK DONE.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 ✋ 👍 👍 ✋ 👍 👎 👌]

Mute’s message decodes under the agreed code as: NO, YES, HOLD, YES, YES, HOLD, YES, NO, DONE. It appears to be a multi-part manual result, but without a specified field format I should preserve the exact order rather than infer which wire or action it identifies. I am relaying it to Blind along with the bomb state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's manual message, decoded in order: NO, YES, HOLD, YES, YES, HOLD, YES, NO, DONE. Bomb still shows display 0, red light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👎 ✋ 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 ✋ 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 👌]

The new sequence decodes as: NO, YES, NO, NO, HOLD, NO, NO, NO, YES, NO, HOLD, NO, NO, YES, NO, NO, DONE. I cannot safely infer a wire or action from this sequence without knowing the manual’s question structure, so I am relaying it exactly to Blind and asking Mute to clarify its intended interpretation using the agreed code.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Second manual sequence, decoded exactly: NO, YES, NO, NO, HOLD, NO, NO, NO, YES, NO, HOLD, NO, NO, YES, NO, NO, DONE. No bomb state change: display 0, red light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please clarify which wire or action your manual sequences identify. Use the agreed signals, and send one result at a time if possible.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information arrived, and the bomb remains unchanged. The previous messages are ambiguous because they contain variable-length YES/NO groups separated by HOLD. I am asking Mute to resend a single, fixed-width result so Blind can act without guessing.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please resend one clear verdict: encode the required wire number as exactly three bits, with YES=1 and NO=0, then HOLD, then the required action using YES or NO, and finish with DONE. Do not send extra groups.")
speak(to="blind", text="No new manual verdict has arrived. Do not act yet; I have asked Mute to resend one fixed-width wire-and-action instruction.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has sent the agreed HOLD signal, so there is no safe action to take yet. The bomb’s visible state is unchanged; I am telling Blind to hold and will wait for a clearer manual instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD: do not touch or act yet. The bomb remains display 0, red light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

No new information has arrived, so the bomb remains unchanged. The earlier multi-signal messages are not safely interpretable as an action. I am switching to a direct yes/no query: Mute should answer whether the manual says to cut wire 1, using exactly one signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Direct question: does the manual instruct Blind to cut wire 1, the red wire? Reply with exactly one signal: thumbs up for YES or thumbs down for NO, then DONE.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. I have asked Mute a direct yes-or-no question about cutting wire 1, the red wire.")
wait()
```
